subject: Define vector of integers in Parameters block

messages.author: e751b45c437d9866
messages.subject: Define vector of integers in Parameters block
parts:
Hi everyone! 

I'm trying to model a Hidden Markov model using STAN. In particular, the observed variables N and C depend on the latent states which is referred as stat. My problem is the following: I need to initialise the vector of the latent integer states "stat" in the parameters block (in fact, I then need to sample each new state from a categorical variable, and the function categorical returns an integer output). However, STAN will not allow me to do so, as the following error message can prove: 

Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'model' with error message:
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:
integer parameters or transformed parameters are not allowed;  found declared type int, parameter name=stat
Problem with declaration.

ERROR at line 27
 25:      vector[s*s-s] mu;
 26:      vector[k*s*s-s] beta_v;
 27:      int <lower=1,upper=s> stat[n_tot];
                                           ^
 28:    }


Here is the original code (the important parts are underlined in gray):

data {
  int<lower=1> n; 
  int<lower=1> n_tot
  int<lower=1> k;   
  int<lower=1> s;               
  int<lower=1> T[n];             
  int<lower=1> T_in[n];         
  matrix<lower=0>[n_tot,k] X;   
  matrix<lower=0>[n_tot,k+1] Z;  
  int<lower=0> N[n_tot];      
  int<lower=0,upper=1> C[n_tot];
  simplex[s] pi_init[s];   
}

parameters {
  row_vector[s] eta;
  vector[k*s] tau_v;
  row_vector[s] alpha;
  vector[k+1*s] gamma_v;
  vector[s*s-s] mu;
  vector[k*s*s-s] beta_v;
  int <lower=1,upper=s> stat[n_tot];
}

transformed parameters {
  matrix[k,s] tau;
  matrix[k+1,s] gamma;
  matrix[k,s*s-s] beta;

  matrix<lower=0>[n_tot,s] lambda;
  matrix<lower=0,upper=1>[n_tot,s] m;
  matrix<lower=0,upper=1>[n_tot,s*s] q;

  {int T_act;  

  for (i in 1:n){
    for (t in 1:T[i]){
      T_act <- T_in[i-1]+t;
      lambda[T_act] <- eta + X[T_act] * tau;
      m[T_act,1]    <- inv_logit(alpha[1] + (Z[T_act] * gamma)[1]);
      m[T_act,2]    <- inv_logit(alpha[2] + (Z[T_act] * gamma)[2]);
      m[T_act,3]    <- inv_logit(alpha[3] + (Z[T_act] * gamma)[3]);
      q[T_act,1] <- 1/(1 + exp(mu[1] + X[T_act] * col(beta,1)) + exp(mu[2] + X[T_act] * col(beta,2)));
      q[T_act,2] <- exp(mu[1] + X[T_act] * col(beta,1))/(1 + exp(mu[1] + X[T_act] * col(beta,1)) + exp(mu[2] + X[T_act] * col(beta,2)));
      q[T_act,3] <- exp(mu[2] + X[T_act] * col(beta,2))/(1 + exp(mu[1] + X[T_act] * col(beta,1)) + exp(mu[2] + X[T_act] * col(beta,2)));
      q[T_act,4] <- exp(mu[3] + X[T_act] * col(beta,3))/(1 + exp(mu[3] + X[T_act] * col(beta,3)) + exp(mu[4] + X[T_act] * col(beta,4)));
      q[T_act,5] <- 1/(1 + exp(mu[3] + X[T_act] * col(beta,3)) + exp(mu[4] + X[T_act] * col(beta,4)));
      q[T_act,6] <- exp(mu[4] + X[T_act] * col(beta,4))/(1 + exp(mu[3] + X[T_act] * col(beta,3)) + exp(mu[4] + X[T_act] * col(beta,4)));
      q[T_act,7] <- exp(mu[5] + X[T_act] * col(beta,5))/(1 + exp(mu[5] + X[T_act] * col(beta,5)) + exp(mu[6] + X[T_act] * col(beta,6)));
      q[T_act,8] <- exp(mu[6] + X[T_act] * col(beta,6))/(1 + exp(mu[5] + X[T_act] * col(beta,5)) + exp(mu[6] + X[T_act] * col(beta,6)));
      q[T_act,9] <- 1/(1 + exp(mu[5] + X[T_act] * col(beta,5)) + exp(mu[6] + X[T_act] * col(beta,6)));
    }
  }
  }
}

model {
  // Priors
  eta ~ normal(0,10);
  tau_v ~ normal(0,10);
  alpha ~ normal(0,10);
  gamma_v ~ normal(0,10);
  mu ~ normal(0,10);
  beta_v ~ normal(0,10);

  {int T_act;

  // Likelihood
  for (i in 1:n){
    T_act <- T_in[i-1]+1;
    stat[T_act] ~ categorical(pi_init);
    N[T_act] ~ poisson(lambda[T_act,stat[T_act]]);
    C[T_act] ~ bernoulli(m[T_act,stat[T_act]]);
    for (t in 2:T[i]){
      T_act <- T_in[i-1]+t;
      stat[T_act] ~ categorical(q[stat[T_act-1]]);
      N[T_act] ~ poisson(lambda[T_act,stat[T_act]]);
      C[T_act] ~ bernoulli(m[T_act,stat[T_act]]);
    }
  }
  }
}


Is there a way to initialise an integer vector in the parameters block? I solved the same issue for the variable T_act by declaring it in curly brackets (local scope), but I can't do it in this case. 

Thank you

Giorgio

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Define vector of integers in Parameters block
parts:
Stan doesn't support sampling over integer parameters. That's
why there's no way to declare an integer parameter.

The manual has a section on how to implement HMMs in Stan.
You need to marginalize out the integer parameters. That'll
still let you estimate emission and transition probabilities.
I haven't worked on really making it efficient, though.

- Bob
